title: Staged reservation handshake and fleet-commitment lifecycle
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers requesting Dedicated capacity currently experience long lead times and opaque approval steps for throughput guarantees and autoscaling controls. We need a repeatable, auditable provisioning workflow that ties reservation requests to a staged handshake (customer <-> sales/solutions), automated capacity checks, and an approval gating system that outputs a machine-readable commitment object for downstream orchestration.
scope: Design the end-to-end reservation-to-deploy lifecycle including: 1) reservation intake form and validation rules, 2) staged SLA negotiation message templates, 3) automated capacity eligibility checks (fleet availability, regional constraints), 4) approval matrix with delegated approvers and escalation, 5) minting of a capacity-commitment object used by provisioning automation and billing, 6) post-provisioning health checks and a 14-day decommitment window for early adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form captures required fields: requested throughput (tokens/s), peak pattern, retention window, legal/regulatory flags, and preferred region
Automated eligibility check returns pass/fail with reasons and suggested alternatives (model quantization, burst credits, alternate region)
Approval matrix enforces delegated approvals (Solutions Eng for <100k tps-min, Sales + Infra for >=100k tps-min) and records approver and timestamp
Capacity-commitment object (JSON manifest) is generated and consumable by provisioning API: includes committed tps, start/end windows, autoscale policy ref, and rollback policy
Provisioning automation can deploy reservation within SLO of 48 hours for standard requests and 2 weeks for large fleet commitments
Dashboard shows reservation lifecycle state and forecasted utilization for first 30 days
Recovery policy and fallbacks documented and tested in staging (automatic fallback to compatible model variant and burst-credit draining)
Customer acceptance test: sample customer is onboarded end-to-end and observes latency and throughput within agreed SLA for first 30 days
out_of_scope: Permanent changes to billing engine, deep changes to fleet autoscaler internals beyond policy configuration; these will be handled in separate engineering epics.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-off: aggressive pre-allocation reduces cold start risk but increases idle-cost; prefer a hybrid model with short warm-up buffer + burst credits
Trade-off: strict single approver reduces time to provision but increases risk underestimation; use delegated matrix with auto-escalation to balance speed and governance
We will initially limit supported regions for fast rollout to US-West and EU-Central, expanding as capacity visibility improves
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize intake schema and approval matrix; design capacity-commitment manifest
Week 2: Implement server-side eligibility checks and prototype 'commitment' minting endpoint
Week 3: Wire approval UI with notifications and audit log; integrate with provisioning automation in staging
Week 4: Pilot with two customers (one mid-market, one enterprise); collect metrics, iterate on templates and thresholds
Week 5: Production rollout to self-serve reservations with visibility toggles for Sales-managed requests
metrics_for_success: Time from reservation submitted to 'committed' state <= 72 hours for standard requests
Provisioning success rate >= 98% on first attempt
Customer NPS for Dedicated onboarding >= +40 for pilot customers
Reduction in manual approval back-and-forth emails by 70%
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Under-provisioning leading to SLA violations; Mitigation: conservative default buffer + mandatory stress test before handoff
Risk: Approval bottlenecks during peak quarter; Mitigation: temporary delegation and auto-approve thresholds for low-risk flows
Risk: Fleet visibility gaps (inaccurate capacity signals); Mitigation: add quick health-check probe and fallbacks to alternate region or lower-quality model variant
